newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan hopes to confirm G7 forex cooperation-source.
newsitem.headline: Japan hopes to confirm G7 forex cooperation-source.

text.p: Japan hopes to confirm its cooperative ties with other Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations in foreign exchange markets in order to achieve currency stability, an international monetary source said on Monday.

"For Japan, it is desirable for currencies to be stable. For that reason, we hope that the monetary authorities will be able to confirm our cooperative stance," the source told Reuters when asked what the G7 nations were going to say on currencies at the G7 summit, which will be held in Denver from June 20-22.

He added that the G7 nations share the view that currency rates should reflect economic fundamentals. They also share the view that excessive volatility in the foreign exchange market is undesirable, the international monetary source said.

Asked whether he thought the dollar's fall to as low as 111.80 yen in Tokyo on Monday was excessive, he said it was difficult to comment on this, as it would depend largely on how one defines "excessive" in the currency market.
Asked whether the dollar/yen rate reflected economic fundamentals, the source said it was necessary to watch the foreign exchange market for a while to determine that.
"Monetary authorities are always in close contact (over currencies)," the source said.
He also did not see Japan's trade and services surplus expanding drastically in the medium to longer term, although the figure may fluctuate from month to month.
On the outlook for the Japanese economy, "There is no change in the trend of the economic recovery becoming firmer centring on private-sector demand," the source said.
The drop in Japan's April household spending was within expectations and the negative impact from the increase in Japan's consumption tax was not likely to linger, the source added.
Japan raised the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
